app.name: Slack app (Slack API / Slack Developer Platform)

verdict.summary: Creating a Slack app and connecting your own workspace takes minutes with no review. Installing into other workspaces needs distribution turned on, which Slack does without review. A Marketplace listing is the hard part: it needs 10+ active installs, a multi-week review, and a trimmed scope set, because Composio's default scopes include restricted search scopes.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 1-2 hours for Gate 1 and 2 setup; 1-3 days to assemble Marketplace listing assets and submission
verdict.time_to_first_connection: About 15-30 minutes once signed in to api.slack.com/apps (estimate)
verdict.approval_wait: None for own-workspace use or unlisted distribution. Marketplace: preliminary review up to 10 business days, then functional review up to 10 weeks for new submissions (current docs; older pages differ).

gates.name: Own workspace (development)
gates.unlocks: Your app can be installed and used in the single workspace that owns it. You can connect your own Slack account through Composio.
limits: Undistributed apps can only be installed in the workspace where they were created; other workspaces fail with invalid_team_for_non_distributed_app.
Access tokens do not expire by default.
Redirect URLs must use HTTPS and cannot contain an anchor.
gates.time_to_reach: Minutes after you sign in to api.slack.com/apps

gates.name: Unlisted distribution (shareable install link)
gates.unlocks: Other workspaces can install the app through an Add to Slack button or install URL. Slack does not list the app in the Marketplace. No review is required.
limits: Commercially distributed unlisted apps get conversations.history at 1 request per minute and 15 objects per request, unless approved for the Marketplace.
Some workspaces only let admins authorize apps, so installs may need admin approval.
Your app must serve SSL for its OAuth redirect URLs and its interaction, options-load and Events API request URLs.
Adding scopes later requires every workspace to reinstall the app.
If you turn on token rotation, access tokens expire every 12 hours and cannot be switched back off.
Slack's docs describe no user cap or warning screen for unlisted apps. Its docs recommend the Marketplace for commercial distribution.
gates.time_to_reach: Minutes after you complete the distribution checklist and click Activate Public Distribution (community source says it takes effect immediately)

gates.name: Slack Marketplace listing
gates.unlocks: Apps appear in the Slack Marketplace, can be installed directly from the listing, and are not subject to the unlisted rate limit on conversations.history.
limits: Requires at least 10 active workspaces (used in the past 28 days) and that threshold must hold for the whole review.
Once published, the live app is locked. Scope, redirect or config changes need a new submission.
Once listed, distribution cannot be switched off with the normal toggle; the listing must be discontinued.
Free-tier workspaces limit message and file history to 90 days.
gates.time_to_reach: Up to 10 business days (preliminary) plus up to 10 weeks (functional) for new submissions, after 10+ active installs are in place

steps.title: Sign in and create the Slack app
steps.detail: Sign in at api.slack.com/apps; the portal will not let you create an app until you are signed in. Create a new app in the workspace you want to own it. Account prerequisites (paid plan, admin role, developer program) were not confirmed by the findings, so check if creation is blocked.
gotchas: Undistributed apps can only be installed in the workspace that owns them until distribution is turned on.

steps.title: Copy the client ID and client secret
steps.detail: Open Basic Information and find App Credentials. Copy the Client ID and Client Secret. You will paste these into your Composio Slack auth config.
gotchas: Keep the client secret out of source control.

steps.title: Register the Composio callback as a Redirect URL
steps.detail: Open OAuth & Permissions and add the Redirect URL under the Redirect URLs section. The URL must use HTTPS and must not contain an anchor. The redirect_uri sent by the authorize call must match this value or be a subdirectory of it.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Composio's default redirect (backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add) and the callback shown in a probe (api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback) differ. Use the one shown in your Composio auth config.
If you register several Redirect URLs, Composio must send the same redirect_uri in both the authorize and token steps, or Slack returns bad_redirect_uri.

steps.title: Trim the scope set before connecting
steps.detail: Do not reuse Composio's default Slack scope list unchanged if the app will ever go to the Marketplace. Draft a scope list that includes only features you will build and test, and remove search:read and search:read.* first. Bot scopes go in the scope parameter as a comma-separated list; user scopes go in user_scope.
gotchas: Scopes are additive per installation and cannot be removed from an existing token without revoking it.
Do not submit scopes for features you have not built yet.

steps.title: Connect your own Slack account through Composio
steps.detail: In Composio, create a Slack auth config that uses your own Client ID and Client Secret, then connect your Slack account to it. Composio's managed OAuth app is an alternative for internal or pilot use. The Composio UI labels were not verified by the findings.
gotchas: Authorization codes expire ten minutes after issue, so complete the exchange promptly.
Do not enable PKCE for this setup unless you have confirmed Composio can exchange codes without a secret. PKCE makes the app a public client and cannot be reversed without Slack support.

steps.title: Test the install in your own workspace
steps.detail: Run an authorization from Composio into the workspace that owns the app. Confirm the token works, then test every scope you requested. Slack's docs say apps must demonstrate use of all scopes, including optional ones.
gotchas: Access tokens do not expire by default. If you later turn on token rotation, tokens expire every 12 hours.

steps.title: Turn on unlisted distribution
steps.detail: Open Manage Distribution. Complete every item in the checklist under Share Your App with Other Workspaces, then click Activate Public Distribution. No review step is listed for unlisted distribution.

values.label: Menu
values.value: Manage Distribution > Share Your App with Other Workspaces > Activate Public Distribution

gotchas: Once distribution is on, the app gets an Add to Slack button and a shareable install URL.

steps.title: Confirm SSL on every public URL
steps.detail: Confirm that every URL Slack calls is served over SSL: the OAuth redirect URL, and any interaction, options-load and Events API request URLs. Test the redirect against the Composio callback before you share the install link.
gotchas: Apps that are distributed must support SSL for all listed URLs.

steps.title: Decide on token rotation before production
steps.detail: Decide whether to enable token rotation. It is opt-in and available only to apps using granular permissions. Once enabled, it cannot be turned off, and access tokens then expire every 12 hours with a single-use refresh token. Your refresh logic must store the new refresh token on every refresh. To convert an existing token, call oauth.v2.exchange with your client ID and secret. For unlisted apps, enable rotation under OAuth & Permissions.
steps.est_time: 1-2 hours to build and test refresh logic
gotchas: Repeated refreshes in one 12-hour window are capped at two active tokens; the oldest extra token is revoked.
Rotation can be turned on for a published app without directory review.

steps.title: Test an install in a second workspace
steps.detail: Install the app in a second workspace using the Add to Slack button or install URL. Admin-restricted workspaces may block the install until an admin approves it. Check that the install completes and that the token works.
gotchas: Installs into workspaces other than the owner fail with invalid_team_for_non_distributed_app if distribution is off.
conversations.history is limited to 1 request per minute for commercially distributed unlisted apps.

steps.title: Prepare Marketplace listing assets and policy pages
steps.detail: Write a short description of 10 words or fewer and a long description. Prepare an icon and at least one 1600x1000 px .jpg or .png under 2 MB. Record a 30-90 second demo video and host it on a public YouTube link (not a channel or playlist). Publish a privacy policy page with a contact by email or web form, a support page, and a publicly accessible landing page with an install path, a post-install confirmation page, and a privacy policy link.
gotchas: A physical address alone does not satisfy the privacy policy requirement.
The support page must give a contact that needs no extra account, with responses within 2 business days.
Direct install from the listing needs a URL that returns an HTTP 302 redirect to a fully qualified slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize URL.

steps.title: Trim scopes and write a reason for each
steps.detail: Draft a reason for each scope that explains how the app uses it, not just what it does. Remove search:read and search:read.* unless they are essential, and expect enhanced review for search:read.*, files:read and *:history scopes. Remove admin.* scopes unless you are in Slack's partner program. Remove user-token scopes unless the app has a clear reason to act as the user.
gotchas: Unnecessary user-token scopes are returned in review.
Enhanced review applies to extensive workspace data access and bot self-add to private conversations.

steps.title: Confirm the Marketplace install threshold and gather installs
steps.detail: Check the live install threshold on the submission page in your app settings before you plan. You need at least 10 active workspaces (used in the past 28 days) and the app must stay at or above that count for the whole review. Get the installs first, because submissions are rejected below this number.

values.label: Threshold
values.value: 10 active workspaces (confirm on the submission page)

gotchas: Older changelogs said 5 active workspaces; the 2026 changelog sets 10 again.
Apps are rejected if they have fewer than 10 active workspaces and fewer than 10 weekly active users.

steps.title: Submit to the Slack Marketplace
steps.detail: Open the Submit to the Slack Marketplace section of the app configuration page. Enter the listing info, scopes with reasons, and test-access details. Reviewers need the app production-ready with test credentials and dummy data. They do not use your own test workspace. Include the demo video of install, OAuth, setup, end-to-end use and uninstall.
gotchas: Changes to published apps (scopes, redirects, config) need a new submission and may need a staging app identical to the live app.
Do not submit scopes for features you have not built yet.

steps.title: Wait for review and respond to feedback
steps.detail: Slack runs a preliminary review of up to 10 business days, then a functional review of up to 10 weeks for new submissions (6 weeks for resubmissions of published apps). Resubmitting during the preliminary review resets your place in the queue. Once a reviewer is assigned in the functional review, resubmitting keeps your place.
steps.est_time: Up to 10 business days + up to 10 weeks
gotchas: An install requesting scopes not yet approved for a published app fails with unapproved_scope.

requirements.item: Redirect URL on HTTPS, no anchor, matched by redirect_uri
requirements.detail: The Composio callback must be registered on OAuth & Permissions. The redirect_uri sent must equal or be a subdirectory of it, and must be identical in the authorize and token steps if several URLs exist.

requirements.item: Own-workspace install only until distribution is on
requirements.detail: Undistributed apps install only in the owning workspace. Other workspaces fail with invalid_team_for_non_distributed_app.
Complete every item under Share Your App with Other Workspaces in Manage Distribution, then click Activate Public Distribution. No review is listed.
OAuth redirect URLs and interaction, options-load and Events API URLs must be served over SSL for a distributed app.

requirements.item: Admin approval may be required by workspace
requirements.detail: Some workspaces only let admins authorize apps, or only allow Marketplace-listed apps. Plan for admin approval during installs.
Access tokens expire every 12 hours with a refresh token. Rotation cannot be turned off. Refresh tokens are single-use. Store every new refresh token.

requirements.item: PKCE is one-way and sets 30-day refresh expiry
requirements.detail: Enabling PKCE makes the app a public client, reversible only through Slack support, and refresh tokens then expire after 30 days. Do not enable it unless you have confirmed Composio's exchange flow works without a secret.
At least 10 active workspaces (used in the past 28 days), maintained through the whole review. Confirm the live value on the submission page.
Short description of 10 words or fewer, long description, icon, 1600x1000 image under 2MB, and a 30-90 second YouTube video (public link, not a channel or playlist).
Cover what data is collected, how it is used, retention, and how a person can request access, transfer or deletion. Provide a contact by email or web form.

requirements.item: Marketplace: support page and public landing page
requirements.detail: Support contact needs no extra account and a response within 2 business days. The landing page must be public (not behind login) and include an install path, a post-install page and a privacy-policy link.

requirements.item: Marketplace: test access and demo video
requirements.detail: Reviewers need production-ready app, test credentials and dummy data; they will not use your own test workspace. A short demo video covering install, OAuth, setup, use and uninstall is requested.

requirements.item: Marketplace: scope reasons and privacy model
requirements.detail: Each scope needs a stated reason. Apps must not expose private channel information to non-members, and must not send users to content they cannot already reach in Slack.

scopes.scope: search:read and search:read.* (files, im, mpim, private, public, users)
scopes.effect: Named as restricted for Marketplace listing and as enhanced review. Composio's defaults include these. Remove them unless essential; a Marketplace app should not reuse Composio's defaults unchanged.
files:read is named as an enhanced-review scope. Requires a clear use and reason in the submission.
*:history scopes are named as enhanced-review. Broad message history needs a clear use case; free-tier history is capped at 90 days.
Named as restricted for listed apps. Admin-level scopes are unlikely to be approved for Marketplace apps unless you are in Slack's partner program.
Only request user scopes if the app has a clear reason to act as the authenticating user. Unnecessary user-token scopes are returned in review.

Adding scopes to an installed app needs each workspace to reinstall. On a published app, an install requesting an unapproved scope fails with unapproved_scope, and the live app needs a new submission.

blockers.symptom: invalid_team_for_non_distributed_app when installing into another workspace
blockers.cause: The app is undistributed and can only be installed where it was created.
blockers.fix: Complete the checklist under Share Your App with Other Workspaces in Manage Distribution, then click Activate Public Distribution.

blockers.cause: The redirect_uri in the authorize step differs from the one in the access step, or does not match a configured Redirect URL.
blockers.fix: Register the exact Composio callback as a Redirect URL and send the same value in both steps.

blockers.symptom: Install blocked or pending admin approval in a workspace
blockers.cause: The workspace only lets admins authorize apps, or only allows Marketplace-listed apps.
blockers.fix: Ask a workspace admin to approve the app, or list it in the Marketplace.

blockers.symptom: conversations.history heavily throttled for a commercial unlisted app
blockers.cause: Since May 29, 2025, commercially distributed unlisted apps are limited to 1 request per minute and 15 objects per request, unless Marketplace-approved. Rollout dates conflict (September 2025 on Slack's page, March 3, 2026 in a community post).
blockers.fix: Batch or cache reads, or pursue Marketplace approval if you need higher limits. The limit was only verified for conversations.history and conversations.replies.

blockers.symptom: Marketplace submission rejected for too few installs
blockers.cause: Fewer than 10 active workspaces and fewer than 10 weekly active users.
blockers.fix: Build installs first, then submit. Confirm the live threshold on the submission page.

blockers.symptom: Marketplace review returns the submission for unnecessary scopes
blockers.cause: Scopes lack a stated reason, are unused, or are restricted (search:read.*, admin.*, user scopes without need).
blockers.fix: Remove unused scopes, write a reason for each, and resubmit. Resubmitting during the preliminary review resets your queue position.

blockers.symptom: Install fails with unapproved_scope on a published app
blockers.cause: The install requests scopes not yet approved for the published app.
blockers.fix: Submit the scope change as a new submission and wait for approval; reinstall after approval.

composio.note: Start on Composio's managed Slack OAuth for internal or pilot use; it needs no app of your own. Register your own Slack app if you need your own branding, your own scope set, a Marketplace listing, or your own rate-limit status. For a Marketplace app, trim Composio's default scopes first: search:read and search:read.* are named as restricted, and files:read and *:history may trigger enhanced review. Composio's redirect URI must be registered as a Redirect URL on your Slack app; this is inferred from Slack's redirect rules and not tested.

Review timelines differ: an older api.slack.com guide says about 1 week preliminary and 7 weeks functional; current docs say 10 business days and 10 weeks (6 weeks for resubmissions). This guide uses the current docs.

The rate-limit rollout date for existing non-Marketplace installs conflicts: September 2, 2025 (Slack) vs March 3, 2026 (community). The rate limit was verified only for conversations.history and conversations.replies.
Whether PKCE-enabled apps can still exchange codes with a client secret was not tested; Composio's use of a secret is an assumption.
Whether Socket Mode app-level tokens (xapp-) need extra steps under token rotation was not checked.
Composio's default scope list was checked against Slack's enhanced-review list only for search:read; files:read and *:history are also flagged as enhanced-review, and other defaults were not checked.
Composio's own UI labels for creating a custom Slack auth config were not verified.
